title: Intel confirms Nova Lake on 18A-P as server demand reshapes factory plans
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Intel has confirmed that Nova Lake will be its first client processor family to use the enhanced Intel 18A-P manufacturing process, with further details promised at CES in January 2027.

Speaking during Intel’s third-quarter earnings presentation, chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said Nova Lake was progressing ahead of schedule. He also said expected design wins at launch would be twice those of Panther Lake, signalling broader adoption by computer manufacturers.

Intel 18A-P builds on the company’s 18A technology through improvements to transistors, interconnects and design optimisation. Intel claims nine percent higher performance at the same power, or 18 percent lower power at equivalent performance. These are process-level comparisons, however, rather than confirmed performance gains for finished Nova Lake processors.

The announcement does not establish that every Nova Lake tile will use Intel’s process. Detailed manufacturing allocations and final product specifications remain undisclosed, leaving CES as the next opportunity for clarification.

Meanwhile, Intel is redirecting manufacturing resources toward server processors. Chief financial officer Dave Zinsner said some Oregon capacity intended for 18A-based Panther Lake chips would be taken offline and converted to Intel 3 production, supporting additional data-centre output. The extra capacity is expected to become productive during the second half of 2027.

Granite Rapids uses Intel 3, making the change a conversion of manufacturing resources between processes, rather than production of Granite Rapids on 18A. Intel says Granite Rapids is already among its fastest-ramping server products, while server demand continues to exceed available supply.

The shift reflects diverging markets: AI infrastructure is strengthening demand for server CPUs, while expensive memory and constrained customer budgets are weakening PC purchases. Intel is therefore adjusting factory priorities while continuing its client roadmap, balancing immediate server opportunities against the capacity needed for future consumer products as market conditions evolve.

Three main Intel processor families are shipping on the original 18A process, as of November 2026:

Intel’s product announcements and latest earnings remarks confirm these families and their production status. This counts processor families, rather than individual CPU models or laptop designs. intel.com

Two additional announced families use the enhanced 18A-P process: Nova Lake for client PCs and Diamond Rapids for servers. Those are separate from the three original 18A families. d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net
